paragraph_content.content: Mix should improve from shift to higher margin trims at F Blue: We think Ford should see a continued mix benefit as production shifts toward higher-margin trims, including the Ranger Raptor, Explorer Tremor, and potentially higher V8 penetration on the F-150. Ford had been under-producing certain margin-accretive products relative to demand given the prior regulatory backdrop, and we expect management to lean further into its truck/SUV profit pools as constraints ease. We think this reinforces Ford's exposure to the right North America profit pools, while Ford's middle-upper income truck/SUV customer base appears relatively resilient despite the recent period of higher gas prices.

Expect Novelis recovery to support production and soften costs: We think the Novelis, Ford's key aluminum supplier, Oswego plant recovery following a fire should lessen recent production volatility for Ford's high margin F-Series. Novelis' restart appears largely in line with Ford's expectations. This should help reduce reliance on alternatively sourced aluminum, where Ford expects a $1.5-$2.0bn headwind. Ford's F-Series production also appears to be improving, with May production the highest year-to-date.

BESS opportunity offers diversification into faster growing end market: We think customer announcements related to Ford's new battery energy storage system (BESS) offering could be a strong catalyst. We believe Ford is likely to emerge as a credible BESS competitor in a market where hardware differentiation is limited, but demand remains strong across utilities, data centers, and large C&I customers. Tesla remains the benchmark with Megapack, but Ford should benefit from strong brand recognition, its
commercial footprint, and a manufacturing/supply-chain strategy designed to align with ITC and domestic-content requirements, which can reduce eligible project costs by ~30%-40%.

Software and services add high-margin growth lever: We think Ford's software and physical services business offers another high-margin growth lever, with management targeting 8% annual revenue growth through 2030 off a ~$15bn base in 2025. While Ford Pro represents the majority of current revenue, we see potential for growth to become increasingly weighted toward Ford Blue as BlueCruise expands across more vehicles and functionality advances toward eyes-off autonomy beginning in 2028. Ford also sees opportunity to take share in parts from independents by expanding its catalogue and refining pricing, which could help reduce the perceived premium to consumers while supporting higher-margin recurring revenue.

paragraph_content.content: F2Q should support a better F3Q setup: IBM guided F2Q constant-currency revenue growth to be similar to F26 of >5%, with operating pre-tax margin expansion of ~50bps as software mix and productivity are partly offset by Confluent dilution. We expect F2Q to be broadly consistent with this framework, with the potential for modest upside from better Software growth, including Data / Confluent and continued Automation strength, with slight acceleration in Red Hat (lapping tougher comps). Consulting expectations remain low but potential for stronger than guided growth in the 2H as enterprise AI adoption accelerates. Infrastructure trends should benefit from demand across Power, Storage, and broader hybrid infrastructure. A solid F2Q would help reinforce the durability of IBM's model and leave the company better positioned into 3Q.

Software concerns look overdone given IBM's portfolio: Recent software pressure has centered on whether agentic AI could disrupt traditional application software, but IBM's portfolio is tied to the infrastructure layer of enterprise IT which should benefit from agentic AI/enterprise AI adoption due to complexity created by more models, agents, workflows, and data movement across hybrid environments. IBM has emphasized that only a very small portion of its Software portfolio is application-like and we see IBM as better positioned for AI-driven software demand than the broader software pullback has implied.

Consulting concerns overdone relative to the size and setup of the business: Consulting is also only ~15% of IBM, so treating the recent pressure as evidence of a broader IBM demand issue appears too punitive, particularly given signings returned to growth in 1Q and AI is already embedded across a meaningful portion of backlog.

Quantum provides an underappreciated catalyst: Quantum should become a more visible part of the IBM story as interest increases (given recent pure-play Quantum IPOs). IBM reiterated in F1Q that it remains on track to deliver its first large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029 and noted that partners could achieve the first examples of quantum advantage this year using IBM hardware. More recently, IBM and the U.S. Department of Commerce announced an LOI to create Anderon, a standalone U.S. quantum chip foundry supported by a proposed $1bn CHIPS award and a $1bn IBM cash contribution, followed by IBM announcing plans to invest more than $10bn in quantum over the next five years. We view these announcements as material for IBM's quantum leadership to receive greater attention and see IBM's quantum business providing optionality for the stock.

Competitor Arrowhead will have Ph3 Redemplo readout for sHTG in 3Q. The anticipation of the event has been an overhang to IONS stock. We believe IONS' Ph3 data has set a high bar to beat on efficacy, while IONS' benign label has reduced room for Redemplo to differentiate on safety (liver fat). We see sHTG as a large market (~$6bn US) that can accommodate both companies, and we model a split market share between Tryngolza and Redemplo ($3bn peak each).

Two cardiovascular Ph3 readouts in 2H26: IONS will have Ph3 readouts of pelacarsen (partnered with Novartis) in mid/3Q26E and Wainua (CardioTTRansform) partnered with AstraZeneca) in 2H26E (we estimate Sept/Oct). We think the more impactful readout is on CardioTTRansform – the TTR approach has been de-risked by competitors' prior Ph3 successes, but there is an opportunity to broaden the market and differentiate based if sub-group data establish combination with standard of care (tafamidis) offers added clinical benefit. We model $4bn nominal peak sales of Wainua or ~$600m royalty to IONS. On pelacarsen, the Ph3 HORIZON readout was originally expected in 1H25, but the trial delays have been attributed to slower event accrual with no early stoppage after first two interim analyses, raising some questions on Ph3 treatment effect size. The upside/downside for IONS from HORIZON is limited by partnership economics & peak sale constraints.

Additional readouts with upside skewed risk/reward setup: IONS' partner Biogen will present full Ph2 data of diranersen in early Alzheimer's at AAIC (July 12-15). For IONS, we think investor expectations for the program are low, given the topline press release (see our report) offered limited data and the optics of missing the primary endpoint on dose response is mixed. That said, Biogen/Ionis advancing the program to pivotal suggest some option value remains. On Angelman, competitor Ultragenyx will have Ph3 readout in 2H – a positive topline would de-risk IONS' program (similar mechanism) ahead of IONS' Ph3 readout in 2027E, while mixed results could reduce competition considering robustness of IONS' own Ph1/2 data (see our report).

paragraph_content.content: CEO Jaime Dimon extended runway. The announcement of Marianne Lake's retirement, in our view, points to several additional years of Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon at the helm, which we believe will be well received by shareholders. Dimon continues to demonstrate a high level of engagement across the franchise and, in our opinion, remains best positioned to guide the bank through a period of anticipated industry transformation driven by AI adoption and digital asset innovation. This comes alongside an evolving regulatory backdrop that may unlock incremental growth opportunities, albeit with associated risks.

Boost from higher-for-longer rates. JPM is set to benefit from a higher-for-longer rate backdrop, with the Fed no longer expected to deliver cuts and the prior NII headwinds from declining rates now reversing. In earlier rate-cut scenarios, NII came under pressure as asset yields declined faster than liabilities could reprice (e.g., ~83bps YoY decline in IORB implied an ~$2bn drag). With that dynamic shifting (for e.g., given no further changes to the fed funds rate through the end of the year, average IORB decline would be 62 bps), JPM's asset-sensitive balance sheet becomes a key tailwind.

As a result, in a stable or rising rate environment, we think asset yields should reprice faster than interest bearing liabilities and therefore drive NII higher. Importantly, this benefit is concentrated in NII ex. markets, which is viewed as more durable/stickier, supporting both near-term upside and sustained benefits carrying into FY2027 and FY2028 as repricing flows through the balance sheet.

Capital Markets Momentum. JPM is well positioned to benefit from the strong capital markets momentum across its investment banking (M&A, ECM, DCM) and trading businesses. Combined with a normalizing regulatory backdrop should allow management to deploy excess capital towards organic growth opportunities.

Expense Guidance de-risked. JPM's expense outlook remains consistent despite the modest increase to ~$106bn (from $105bn) during the recent Bernstein Conference, with management indicating the step-up is largely driven by stronger underlying revenue performance rather than incremental cost pressure. At the same time, fee income is tracking ahead of expectations. As a result, the combination of relatively stable expenses and improving fee income should drive positive operating leverage, implying upside to net income versus prior expectations.

paragraph_content.content: Option maintenance fees margin headwind will likely rise: LEN has ~$18.5bn of partner capital deployed into controlled lots as of F1Q. These arrangements carry an implied ~10% cost of capital, paid via option maintenance fees (OMFs). While OMFs are paid in cash as incurred, they are capitalized to D&ACORE and only flow through cost of sales when homesites are purchased and delivered. This creates a timing mismatch, with current cash outflows exceeding P&L expense, driving continued growth in D&ACORE (up $237mm QoQ in F2Q, primarily from capitalized OMFs). As Lennar accrues OMFs across a multi-year land pipeline but only expensing costs tied to current deliveries, we believe near-term margins understate the economic burden. We expect this imbalance to narrow as LEN scales its asset-light model, with incremental margin headwind and D&ACORE likely to continue building before stabilizing in ~2 years.

Delivery acceleration could come at the expense of margins: LEN's FY26 guidance of 82k-83k deliveries implies flat to +9% growth in F4Q vs. down (3%) in F3Q at the midpoint. While Lennar remains focused on driving volume through even-flow production and sales pace, we see risk that growth could come at the expense of margins. Market inelasticity is evident amid weaker employment and elevated inventory: F1Q26 absorption was slightly below normal seasonality in an overall choppy market. Gross margin of 15.6% was in-line with guidance, and F3Q GM guidance of approximately 16% is driven by direct cost savings and flattish QoQ incentives. F3Q SG&A of 8.8%-9.0% higher than forecast due to investment in digital marketing and technology platforms.
Financial services operating income guide was also below our expectations due to shift to more adjustable-rate mortgages.

Expect additional 100bps ROTE decline in F26: Following a 670bps YoY decline in LEN's ROTE in F2025 (vs. average builder in our coverage down 520bps), we forecast a 320bps decline in F2026 driven by: 1) accruing OMFs in D& ACORE 2) rising lot costs (estimate 30% of homebuilding sales), 3) net price pressure given affordability headwinds for entry level buyers and higher new/resale home inventory levels in certain markets, and 4) Millrose option fee related to its land spin-off to ramp-up to 70bps/100bps in F2026/F2027. We also see headwinds on SG&A from digital marketing and technology investments.

Incentives still elevated with higher inventory and rates: We expect LEN to continue relying on incentives to support demand, given persistent affordability challenges and elevated mortgage rates, particularly for entry-level buyers.
